public_rationale: On August 7, 2023, San Francisco agencies identified needed improvements in handling emergency scenes, caution tape, cones, wires and human traffic directions [e2]. A city filing described continuing construction-zone difficulties, including a Cruise vehicle becoming stuck in wet concrete on August 15, 2023 [e1]. Together, these records support recurring practical difficulty with unusual road situations during the August 1–19, 2023 assessment period [e1] [e2].
limitations: These San Francisco records do not establish an industry-wide failure rate or quantify failures per encounter with unusual circumstances [e1] [e2].
They do not isolate machine learning as the cause of the reported system-level difficulties [e1] [e2].
The wet-concrete account relies on local reporting rather than a published software investigation [e1].

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Driverless cars still have a problem, which is edge cases: out-of-the-ordinary circumstances that often confound machine learning algorithms.

statement.excerpt: That problem, which I have emphasized dozens of times over the last several years, is edge cases, out-of-the-ordinary circumstances that often confound machine learning algorithms.
statement.document_title: Face it, self-driving cars still haven’t earned their stripes

our_interpretation: The plain reading is that unusual road situations remained a recurring practical difficulty for driverless systems, rather than that most trips failed.
Because this describes an ongoing state and discusses incidents that month, use August 1–19, 2023, the publication month through the post date.
Assess observable driving-system difficulties. Incident reports alone cannot identify which machine-learning component caused a failure.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporaneous incident records and operational assessments show recurring difficulty handling unusual road situations.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative evaluations show that unusual road situations no longer presented a recurring difficulty for operating driverless systems.
